title: ATTRACTED THE FRUIT FLIES, BUT THEY DIDN’T GO INSIDE
body: The fruit flies just sat on the Apple and never went inside.

title: Not Very Effective
body: Frankly unimpressed. Before getting these, I used a bowl with a TBS of sugar, half a cup of warm water and a few tablespoons of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of Dawn. I also have three Zevo insect traps (basically very sticky plastic inside a plug in that has a warm blue light). The bowl traps were far more effective at getting a dozen of the buggers trapped (fruit fly invasion, and I do mean invasion). The "bait" in these apple traps obviously contains apple cider vinegar. But the flys would crawl around on the outside and only a few would actually end up in the trap. These traps are very small, and supposedly last 45 days which is ridiculous. After only a few days, they stopped working completely. The Zevo traps, on the other hand, had well over a hundred flies trapped. I had to change those traps out twice a week (it's normally like a month or two before they have to be changed, but INVASION of fruit flies). They are much more effective.

title: Flies don’t go in?!

title: Not very effective

title: It's just Apple Cider Vinegar in a Cup?
body: Well, I can honestly say I'm shocked at this one. I'm pretty sure this is just Apple Cider Vinegar in a cup. I could've bought an entire quart at the store and made my own traps with 20oz bottles for a fraction of the cost, but here we are. Pros: - well I guess I didn't have to build traps Cons: - There's no lid. Unlike other traditional traps, this is just wide open, so don't knock it over. - Pretty sure it's just ACV in a container, so for the price, it's not really worth it - Haven't caught any fruit flies, which are coming out of my drains. My cup is right on the sink, so I'd think there would be something. We'll see how this goes, but so far, I have to be careful not to spill it, it's just ACV, and I haven't caught any fruit flies, so it's not working. I'll update if something changes.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
body: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

body: Ineffective -- we recently had an issue with fruit flies and this product didn't do its job. Better luck with homemade solution of water, vinegar, and dish soap. Also found sticky traps worked.

body: sadly they do not work - don't know why but I was hoping this took care of my problem but not happening - going back to my local hardware store to get the ones that have worked in the past and these are going back to Amazon

title: Does not work at all!
body: We had a lot of fruit flies upon returning from vacation. We tried these traps and caught only two flies with them in two weeks! The jars do not have any way to trap the flies, the lid is wide open, and this is a flaw of design. If the lid had smaller holes in it, the flies would get trapped in there. The flies fly into these traps and do not stay there--whatever is in it does not attract or kill them. We got rid of our fruit flies using yellow sticky glue traps and other liquid fruit fly traps that have a better attractant and design to keep the flies trapped. And also good old-fashioned home-made vinegar, water, dish soap traps helped--with a dash of apple-cider vinegar as attractant or small piece of fruit in it.

title: Not worth it
body: I purchased this item due to a recommendation by several websites. I had a MUCH better experience catching fruit flies with a home remedy than this product. I tried it in different areas of the kitchen and only caught one. The home remedy caught the large majority of the flies we were struggling with. The home remedy was apple cider vinegar and a drop of dish soap. I learned through trial-and-error that a shot glass works best instead of a bowl. I assume the steeper sides of the glass helped catch them.

title: It is a hit or miss product.
body: This is a hit or miss product. It did not work for me at all. It's a cheap alternative but you risk not having the results you want. Strong vinegar smell. Wouldn't recommend.

title: Great start… then … sad face
body: I do not usually write reviews on products but felt compelled due to my disappointment in this. First- I have had this massive amount of fruit flies that have appeared out of nowhere. I ordered this, as I thought the reviews were great. When first opened, as other products said- wow! That is a strong odor that is not terribly welcoming. But I was thinking that I was more than willing to deal with it if it meant that I was fruit fly free. Sadly, those pesky bugs seemed to have outsmarted the trap and only a fraction of them have lost their life to this product. I somehow think (irrational and though it may be) that this product has somehow made them not only stronger but smarter. If you have a small amount of irritants, this may be helpful. But for a larger swarm, I am looking elsewhere.

title: Smell is Strong and Spreads
body: It makes your whole house smell like vinegar with a hint of sweetness. The smell is very strong and spread throughout the entire house overnight. I had to close it up and run a fan to get rid of the smell. It only caught one gnat overnight, even though there was a light trap in the same room plugged into an outlet (Zevo) that had just caught over 50 gnats in the previous 48 hours.

title: The smell is TERRIBLE
body: I can't tell you if it works or not because the smell is awful. If you like the smell of vinegar airfreshener, then you'll be ok. The next day after opening it, I put the top back on!

title: Poor design, spills easily!
body: I was expecting more for the extra money I spent on this Raid product. Like maybe a liquid product that wouldn't spill stuff all over when I opened it. When I unscrewed the lid, Raid had one of those protective plastic coverings over the opening of the jar that you have to peel back by gripping the extra piece of attached material that's supposed to make it easier to peel, but doesn't actually WORK since it's glued on so firmly. Oh well. OK. So I grabbed a sharp knife and carved away the temporary protective covering, which exposed the jar of apple cider vinegar that is said to kill the fruit flies. For the price, I expected another lid with holes in it to prevent it from spilling when I put it down near my compost pail. But no. It was just a jar of open liquid that had already spilled once when I carved away the protective covering! So I had to place the $8.18 jar of Raid in a sealed plastic sandwich bag with holes in it. I don't know yet how well it works. But here's the issue. If I wanted to create a DIY fruit fly disposal system, I would get my own jar of apple cider vinegar and put it in a sealed sandwich bag with holes in it. AND I would have saved myself $8.18! There are other, better designed fruit fly apple cider products on Amazon that have holes in the lids to prevent spillage. I just expected more from a big brand name like Raid. Silly me.

title: Fruit fly trapper

title: Not effective
body: I bought this with the hopes of catching gnats. It only caught two. I watched the gnats just walk along the rim. I wouldn’t recommend it. I ended up doing baking soda and vinegar in my drain and that worked.

title: Not great.
body: This was not as effective as advertised. It collected a small amount of fruit flies, but it also served as an attractant that they wouldn't touch. I had it open for 2 weeks and the amount of flies only got worse. At the end of the 2 weeks there were maybe 20 in the jar, and still dozens in the air. As soon as I closed the jar, they were gone in about a day. I would not recommend this item. It also smells awful- if using it indoors, prepare for your house to smell like vinegar-soaked work socks.

title: Just apple cider vinegar in a cup !!
body: This is nothing more than apple cider vinegar in a cup! You can Google home fruit fly remedies, and they all suggest to put apples cider vinegar in a cup with A drop of dish soap so that the flies sink into the liquid. Once I open this product, it was clear that it is just apple Cider vinegar that you can put in a cup for less than a quarter. Yes, this is effective, but you can make yourself at home. Don’t spend six dollars on this.

title: Worked decent after awhile
body: Like a lot of reviews have mentioned, I opened this thing up with a decent number of fruit flies around and was having seemingly no success. I went ahead and left it in position near my trash can and after a few days it finally started to catch them. Not sure if they needed time to warm up to it or what, but it works decent these days for a relatively cheap product that doesn't stink up the place TOO bad.

title: Effective but stinky!
body: Effective, but stinky! Got all the critters quickly, but it stinks up the kitchen with strong apple vinegar smell. I have used others before that did not make such a strong smell. Next time I will just buy the little apple shaped ones. Not a great choice in a house with sensitive nosed people, and the container is quite large, always afraid it will get knocked over.

title: Didn't seem to work as effective?

title: So-so

Not sure what's happening there. Appreciate that there is no awful smell and the design doesn't both me sitting out in my kitchen.

title: Works as well as vinegar and dish soap.
body: Works as well as dish soap and apple cidar vinegar or regular white vinegar. More expensive than the mentioned method. The container is cool but you could buy one for cheap. Good option is you do not wish to out the ingredients together yourself and pour into a container. I caught two fruit flies with it, my vinegar and dish soap caught three over a 24 hour period. Could be location of containers. I ended up swatting about 10 of them myself. So get a gooe fly swatter. The flies will land in areas and you can see them and crush their souls.

Does it work? Yes. Do I still have the same type of flies that I had before? Yes, yes I do. Have I tried moving it around where I see flies? Yes, I have. If I had to guess I have 6 flies/gnats, and the bottle has 3 of them. So I gave it a 3/5 rating for getting me 50% of the flies.

title: Has an effect over time, just not immediately
body: Smells like an open jar of red vinegar. No film to trap flying insects in the solution, They basically sit on top of the open jar & nothing precludes the insect from flying away. Maybe it intoxicates them & they fall in & drown. Eventually some bugs do wind up dead at the bottom of in the solution. I did notice a significant decrease in the number of small flying insects in 7-10 days; just not an immediate impact. Cats do not like the vinegar smell & leave it alone wherever you put it (off the floor).

title: Not effective in my experience
body: We tend to get gnats and fruit flies around the kitchen sink, our countertop compost bin, and fruit basket, and we have used a variety of fly traps to control them. I was excited to try these Hot Shot Flying Insect Traps, but so far, I am not seeing a positive effect. First, I was a little concerned about the trap itself. The trap contains a liquid that easily spills, so you have to be careful to place it where it isn't at risk of being knocked over (away from kids and kitties, for example). I placed on of these traps on our kitchen countertop behind the sink and next to prime gnat real estate over ten days ago, but so far, it hasn't caught a single critter. This morning I saw a gnat hovering close to it and thought, "ok, today is the day the fly trap will do its thing." But I checked a few hours later, and still--not a single captured critter. This trap only has a couple more days to perform (the directions say to replace them every two weeks), but I am not too optimistic that I will suddenly see a different outcome from what I've experienced to date. If that changes, I will update my review. But as things stand today, the product is simply not performing as I'd expected.

Not a single thing has been caught, especially not one of these flies that were sent straight from my darkest of nightmares to annoy and piss me off every second of every day. I can't say these definitely don't work at all cause I might have put them on terrible places around the house. I'm staying hopeful that they do work for anyone out there that buys these in the future!

title: Trap Doesn't Attract Flies, Spills, Improvement required - Trap Parts Potentially Useful for DIY
body: Trap Doesn't Catch Flies & Spills Unavoidably! Have been using for over a month - haven't caught a single fly (but have other traps that catch smaller flies just fine). This Trap is really no different from small vinegar based fly traps, but is intended to catch larger flies. The flies are supposed to enter the top grid (should be attracted to the weak detergent mixture inside as it smells like weak vinegar which they like), and are supposed to fall into the dilute detergent mixture in the packet sitting inside, which would kill them. But not only did flies seem to be completely not attracted, unfortunately, but the packets are shaped such that you can't attach or remove the grid/lid, without one side of the detergent packet snaps on the legs of the lid, and spills as you open it. So you end up with much less liquid in the trap, which will dry out quickly. I will be trying out my own apple cider vinegar solutions to try to improve the attraction rate, and possibly will add a small amount of detergent, though that may not be required (will require testing), as there seems to be a real gap in the market for a small non-toxic liquid based trap like this, for larger flies (there are plenty of effective vinegar traps for the small flies already). These traps will be worthwhile if I can at lease reuse the casings ... but not sure I can even get that to work yet.

title: needs help!
body: I bought this product to try to get a fruit fly problems under control. In my office at work a co-worker had left a banana out under her desk that we did not know about. We starting getting loads of fruit flies so I decided to give these traps a try. I bought this one and another brand to do some comparison with. The other brand contained only malic acid. I opened them both at the same time and put them out. Immediately fruit flies started collecting around the rim of both containers but none seemed to want to go inside. I waited overnight and this brand had 3 flies in it the next morning and the other brand had only one. Still had dozens sitting around the top edge of the container but none wanted to enter. I looked back at some of the reviews and found one person had used these in combination with a yellow sticky card and said it was very successful. I tried it and believe me it made all the difference in the world. In a short while I had over 20 stuck to the card that I had placed in the jar. Like I said they will work good but just need a little extra help.
